title: Canonical CITE Blue Lake Basic WMS source lock

licenseEvidence.scope: The license file at the pinned repository root is recorded as the distribution evidence for the pinned archive.
licenseEvidence.review: Provenance and license evidence recorded; this is not legal advice.

preparation.publicationMode: Dry-run by default; explicit --execute uses shared-auth authority and the ordinary authenticated upload, resource, style, render-profile, workflow, WMS-publication, and public-service management APIs. Anonymous GetMap remains exact-prewarmed-cache-only.
preparation.reason: The governed Shapefile ingestion boundary accepts exactly one shapefile dataset per ZIP; the official archive contains several datasets and supporting formats.
preparation.output: One deterministic, flat, four-component Shapefile ZIP per Basic layer plus upload-manifest.json

defaultStyleContract.allLayers: Every prepared layer needs a checksum-pinned render profile before publication.
defaultStyleContract.cite:Lakes: The default polygon fill must contain non-white pixels, as required by the Basic WMS ETS preconditions.

limitations: This source lock and deterministic preparation path now have two byte-identical local reviewed-worker receipts and two byte-identical ten-request production-render-code materializations. They do not mean that the fixture has been uploaded to governed storage, registered in PostgreSQL, publicly served, deployed, interactively judged, or tested by the official ETS.

The ten-request prewarm inventory covers only fixed dataset-specific basic.xml identities; SERVICE-022 resolves the separate always-run request surface against local production Capabilities, while exact deployed profile-version successful-image materialization remains open.
Prepared archives intentionally exclude the upstream GML, MapInfo, raster, metadata, time, and elevation-option assets; those remain future option-specific fixtures.
An operator must use the ordinary authenticated upload and completion endpoints so authorization, object verification, processing, lineage, and audit controls remain in force.

The publication client intentionally requires public resource visibility for the canonical Apache-2.0 fixture, resumes only exact immutable originals, and fails closed on ambiguous identities, byte drift, or an unfinished upload; it has not been executed against AWS or a deployed OpenGeo endpoint.
